chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:
I asked him about a covering made from foxes or Khwārazmī fur: may one perform salat (prayer) in it or not? He said: If it has been properly slaughtered, then there is no objection to it.

So the proper way regarding these reports is that we interpret them as a form of taqiyyah, not as applying in a state of free choice, because that is the doctrine of all the generality, and this confirms what we have already presented.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under certain circumstances
key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes; referring here to fox fur or skin
key_terms.اللِّحَافِ: a covering or wrap used as a garment or blanket
key_terms.الِاخْتِيَارِ: a state of free choice, not compulsion or necessity
key_terms.الْخُوَارَزْمِيَّةِ: Khwārazmī fur or material attributed to Khwārazm
key_terms.ذَكِيًّا: properly slaughtered according to ritual law
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no objection to it; it is not problematic

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in garments or coverings made from fox fur according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling on performing salat (prayer) in a covering made from fox fur or Khwārazmī fur. The final statement explains that such reports are to be understood as issued in taqiyyah, indicating their legal significance must be read in light of broader jurisprudential evidence.
